paragraphs.title: The Statue and the Gathering of the Kingdom

easy.explanation: Nebuchadnezzar the king made the image.
easy.q: Who made the image?

easy.explanation: The image was made of gold.
easy.q: What was the image made of?

easy.explanation: He set it up in the plain of Dura, in the province of Babylon.
easy.q: Where did Nebuchadnezzar set up the image?

answers: To come to the dedication of the image
medium.explanation: The officials were summoned to the dedication of the image.
medium.q: Why did the king send for the officials?

answers: The princes and other rulers of the provinces
medium.explanation: The princes, governors, captains, judges, and other rulers gathered together.
medium.q: Who gathered before the image?

answers: A ceremony of opening or consecration
medium.explanation: The dedication was the ceremony for presenting and consecrating the image.
medium.q: What does “dedication” mean in this passage?

answers: The event was intended to be a broad royal ceremony
The image was small and unimportant
The king wanted to hide the image
challenge.explanation: Gathering officials from throughout the kingdom shows the event’s public importance.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the king’s summoning all the officials?

answers: The gathering caused the image to be made
The gathering was for the dedication of the image
The image was intended to prevent the gathering
challenge.explanation: The officials were called to attend the dedication of the image already set up.
challenge.q: What was the relationship between setting up the image and gathering the officials?

answers: The image belonged equally to every nation
The image had no connection with the king
The king was the initiator and ruler of the ceremony
challenge.explanation: The repetition highlights Nebuchadnezzar’s authority and personal initiative.
challenge.q: What is emphasized by the repeated mention that Nebuchadnezzar set up the image?

paragraphs.title: The Command to Bow and the Threat of the Furnace

easy.explanation: The herald cried aloud the king’s command.
easy.q: Who proclaimed the command?

answers: Fall down and worship the image
easy.explanation: They were commanded to fall down and worship the golden image.
easy.q: What were the people required to do when the music sounded?

answers: Being cast into a burning fiery furnace
easy.explanation: Anyone who refused was to be cast into the fiery furnace.
easy.q: What was the punishment for refusing to worship?

answers: Hearing the sound of the musical instruments
A command from the Chaldeans alone
medium.explanation: The command required worship when the instruments sounded.
medium.q: What caused the people to fall down and worship?

answers: A person who publicly announces something
medium.explanation: A herald is someone who proclaims a message aloud.
medium.q: What is a herald?

answers: To establish the location of the image
To make the people obey the command
medium.explanation: The music marked the time to worship, while the punishment threatened those who refused.
medium.q: Why did the command include both music and punishment?

answers: It applied only to the king
challenge.explanation: The threat of the furnace shows that the king demanded complete obedience.
challenge.q: What does the severe punishment reveal about the command?

answers: The music signaled when worship should begin
challenge.explanation: When the music sounded, the people were to fall down and worship.
challenge.q: What was the relationship between the music and the worship?

answers: The command concerned only a small group
The king intended the command for a wide population
challenge.explanation: The wording includes people from many nations and languages.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the words “people, nations, and languages”?

easy.explanation: Certain Chaldeans came near and accused the Jews.
easy.q: Who came and accused the Jews?

easy.explanation: They reported Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego to the king.
easy.q: Whom did the Chaldeans accuse?

answers: Not serving the king’s gods and not worshipping the image
easy.explanation: The accusation was that they would not serve the king’s gods or worship the image.
easy.q: Of what were the three men accused?

answers: They would not worship the image
medium.explanation: The king had commanded every person to fall down and worship the image.
medium.q: Why was their conduct considered a violation of the king’s command?

medium.explanation: The Chaldeans brought a charge against the three men before the king.
medium.q: What does “accused” mean in this passage?

answers: That the three men were not musicians
That the three men were not Babylonians
That the three men would not serve the king’s gods or worship the image
medium.explanation: They repeated the two acts of disobedience in their report.
medium.q: What detail did the Chaldeans emphasize?

answers: To show that officials were expected to obey the king
To prove that they were musicians
To say that they had no connection with the kingdom
challenge.explanation: They noted that the king had set the men over the affairs of Babylon.
challenge.q: Why did the Chaldeans mention the three men’s positions in Babylon?

answers: They refused every service to the king
They could serve in government without worshipping the king’s gods
challenge.explanation: Their service as officials did not require them to worship the king’s gods.
challenge.q: What can be understood from the difference between their public service and their worship?

answers: It causes the image to disappear
It brings the three men into direct conflict with the king
challenge.explanation: Because of the accusation, Nebuchadnezzar summons the men before him.
challenge.q: How does the accusation advance the story?

easy.explanation: The king was filled with rage and fury.
easy.q: How did Nebuchadnezzar react to the accusation?

easy.explanation: He gave them another chance to worship when the music sounded.
easy.q: What opportunity did the king give the three men?

answers: They would not serve the king’s gods or worship the image
easy.explanation: They firmly declared that they would not worship the image.
easy.q: What did Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego say?

answers: To question them and give them an opportunity to respond
To send them to another province
medium.explanation: The king questioned them directly and offered them another chance to obey.
medium.q: Why did Nebuchadnezzar bring the three men before him?

answers: We do not need to give a defensive answer
medium.explanation: They said they did not need to argue or evade the issue.
medium.q: What does “we are not careful to answer thee in this matter” mean?

answers: They chose loyalty to God over obedience to the image
medium.explanation: They declared that they would serve their God alone and would not worship the image.
medium.q: What was the meaning of the three men’s answer?

answers: Their God could deliver them, but even if He did not, they would not worship
The king had to deliver them
They would be delivered only if the music stopped
challenge.explanation: They trusted God’s power to deliver them but did not make faithfulness depend on rescue.
challenge.q: What condition did the three men place on their deliverance?

answers: They did not know what to do
Their loyalty did not depend on the outcome
They agreed to serve the image
challenge.explanation: Even without deliverance, they would not serve the king’s gods.
challenge.q: What does “but if not” reveal about their faithfulness?

answers: It moves from a question about a command to a refusal to abandon their faith
It moves from an appointment to a musical contest
It moves from war to a peace agreement
challenge.explanation: The king demands worship, but the men declare that they will not forsake their God.
challenge.q: How does the confrontation change at the end of the three men’s speech?

easy.explanation: The king commanded that it be heated seven times more than usual.
easy.q: How many times hotter did the king command the furnace to be heated?

answers: They bound them and cast them into the furnace
They hid them in the palace
easy.explanation: The mighty men bound the three men and cast them into the furnace.
easy.q: What did the soldiers do to the three men?

easy.explanation: The flames killed the soldiers who carried out the king’s command.
easy.q: What happened to the soldiers who cast them in?

answers: Because he was furious at their refusal
Because he wanted to heat the palace
medium.explanation: The unusually intense heat reflected the king’s great fury.
medium.q: Why did the king command the furnace to be heated seven times more?

medium.explanation: The men were tied before they were cast into the furnace.
medium.q: What does “bound” mean in this passage?

answers: The three men were never in the furnace
The fire struck those who cast them in, while the three men were preserved
medium.explanation: The soldiers died from the flames, but the three men were not destroyed by them.
medium.q: What does the death of the soldiers emphasize about the three men’s fate?

answers: The punishers are harmed, while the condemned men remain alive
The three men rescue the soldiers
challenge.explanation: The fire kills the soldiers, while the three men survive inside the furnace.
challenge.q: What reversal occurs in these verses?

answers: It causes him to cancel the punishment
It causes him to intensify the heat and the command
It causes him to worship the image
challenge.explanation: In his fury, he orders extraordinary heat and the men’s execution.
challenge.q: How does the king’s anger affect his actions?

answers: They were part of the musicians
They were sent to punishment with no human means of escape
challenge.explanation: Their restraints and clothing emphasize the severity of the punishment and their helplessness.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the men being cast in with their garments and bound?

paragraphs.title: The Fourth Figure in the Fire

easy.explanation: Nebuchadnezzar saw four men walking in the midst of the fire.
easy.q: How many men did Nebuchadnezzar see in the fire?

answers: They had escaped from the furnace
easy.explanation: They were walking in the fire and had no hurt.
easy.q: What was the condition of the men in the fire?

easy.explanation: The king said the form of the fourth was like the Son of God.
easy.q: What did the fourth figure look like?

answers: He saw four men instead of three, and they were unharmed
medium.explanation: He saw an additional man and observed that none of them had been harmed.
medium.q: What astonished Nebuchadnezzar?

answers: The one in the fourth position
medium.explanation: The word identifies the additional, fourth person in the furnace.
medium.q: What does “fourth” mean?

answers: Come out of the fire and come near him
medium.explanation: He called them to come forth from the furnace.
medium.q: What did Nebuchadnezzar command the three men to do?

answers: Someone else was present with the three men in the fire
The king had mistaken the number of images
challenge.explanation: The king saw four men even though only three had been cast into the furnace.
challenge.q: What does the appearance of the fourth figure show according to the king’s description?

answers: The fire is burning, but the men walk without harm
The furnace is cold, but the men are burned
challenge.explanation: Although the fire is intense, it does not injure the men inside it.
challenge.q: What striking contrast appears in the description of the furnace?

answers: From ordering their execution to calling them out
From protecting them to throwing them in
From indifference to refusing to see them
challenge.explanation: After ordering them into the furnace, he calls them out when he sees they are unharmed.
challenge.q: How does the king’s attitude change at this moment?

answers: The fire had no power over them
easy.explanation: The fire had no power over their bodies.
easy.q: What did the officials see about the bodies of the three men?

answers: The God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego
easy.explanation: The king blessed the God of the three men.
easy.q: Whom did Nebuchadnezzar bless?

answers: He cast the image into the furnace
He promoted the three men in the province of Babylon
easy.explanation: The king promoted Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego in Babylon.
easy.q: What did the king do after their deliverance?

answers: Their hair was not singed, their coats were unchanged, and they had no smell of fire
medium.explanation: Their bodies, hair, clothing, and smell showed no effect of the fire.
medium.q: What signs showed that the fire had not harmed the three men?

medium.explanation: The king said that God had rescued His servants.
medium.q: What does “delivered” mean in this passage?

answers: Because the three men surrendered to him
Because God sent His angel and delivered His servants
medium.explanation: The king attributed their rescue to God’s sending His angel and protecting them.
medium.q: Why did Nebuchadnezzar praise their God?

answers: The deliverance was complete, not merely a narrow escape
The three men were partly burned
The men never entered the furnace
challenge.explanation: There was no remaining sign that the fire had touched them.
challenge.q: What does the examination of their hair, clothing, and smell demonstrate?

answers: From contempt and defiance to recognition of His power
challenge.explanation: After the rescue, the king blesses their God and acknowledges His ability to deliver.
challenge.q: What is the central change in the king’s attitude toward the God of the three men?

answers: To force the three men to worship
To protect the honor of their God and forbid insulting speech against Him
To remove all officials from the province
challenge.explanation: The decree punished anyone who spoke improperly against their God.
challenge.q: What was the purpose of the king’s new decree?

paragraphs.title: Nebuchadnezzar’s Letter about the Most High God

easy.explanation: The proclamation was directed to every people, nation, and language.
easy.q: To whom did Nebuchadnezzar address his proclamation?

answers: The signs and wonders God had done for him
The making of the musical instruments
easy.explanation: He declared the signs and wonders performed by the Most High God.
easy.q: What did Nebuchadnezzar tell them about?

easy.explanation: The passage describes His kingdom as everlasting and His dominion as enduring from generation to generation.
easy.q: How long do the kingdom and dominion of the Most High God last?

answers: The Most High God performs signs and wonders, and His rule is everlasting
The image is more important than God
medium.explanation: The king emphasizes God’s mighty works and eternal kingdom.
medium.q: What is the main message of the proclamation?

medium.explanation: The word describes acts that are mighty and impressive.
medium.q: What does “great” mean in the phrase describing God’s signs and wonders?

answers: They prove that the king is stronger than God
They cause the kingdom to be abolished
They lead to recognition of God’s greatness and everlasting rule
medium.explanation: The wonders lead the king to declare the greatness and permanence of God’s kingdom.
medium.q: How do the signs and wonders relate to the conclusion of the proclamation?

answers: The message about God’s power is presented to a wide audience
The king is hiding the event
The king is speaking only to his court
challenge.explanation: The proclamation makes the testimony about God public throughout the kingdom.
challenge.q: What is the significance of addressing all peoples after the furnace event?

answers: The image was made by the king, while God’s kingdom is described as everlasting
The image is eternal, while God is temporary
There is no difference between them
challenge.explanation: The image is a human creation, but God’s kingdom endures forever.
challenge.q: What contrast exists between the image at the beginning and the Most High God at the end?

answers: It caused him to ignore God
It led him to proclaim God’s greatness and everlasting dominion
It caused him to build another furnace
challenge.explanation: After the deliverance, the king publicly declared the greatness and enduring rule of the Most High God.
challenge.q: How did the furnace event affect the king’s final words?
